assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Use a separate copy. Keep Dock open, change the bay to 9, then swap the two commands. Predict the order before running.
criteria: The number and order change for different reasons.

lab.title: A loading-dock sign
lab.task: Edit the starter. The first line must read Dock open and the second Bay 4. Preserve case, spaces and order. No input is needed.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a copy of your finished program, remove the closing quote temporarily. Record the stage where it stops, restore the quote and change the message to Status: offline.
criteria: Name the stage of each check and compare the final output with the prediction.

lab.title: Build a status indicator
lab.task: Edit the starter main.c until a successful run prints Status: ready. Fix the build with waiting unchanged first. Record what happens, then edit the message.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Make a copy for a different desk. Print Desk "C" and Ticket 11 while leaving the first line alone. Explain why the number of lines stays the same.
criteria: You change the arguments to two calls while preserving the number of commands.

lab.title: A check-in card
lab.task: Print exactly three lines: CHECK IN, Desk "B", Ticket 8. Use three puts calls and the standard main.c structure. The second line contains printed quotation marks.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Make a variant for tray 7 and section C, then change only the volume in a second run. Predict the differences before you run them.
criteria: You can point to the argument that controls each part of the result.

lab.title: A tray label
lab.task: Print Tray 3: 2.50 L (B) followed by Fill: 80% on the next line. Pass the numbers and B as separate printf arguments. No input is needed.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Change only the period to 1.0, then change the line separately. Predict which parts of both lines change in each test.
criteria: Changing one initial value affects its own field in both prints.

lab.title: Track boxes on a loading line
lab.task: Line B starts with 12 boxes and a period of 0.5 hours. Print B: 12 / 0.5 h. Reduce the count by three and print the second line using the same format.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Restore cans = 19. Predict the result, then try (double)(cans / days) in a copy and compare the output.
criteria: The original gives 26 4.75.
The modified version gives 26 4.00.
Name the operation that loses the fraction.

lab.title: A reserve and daily average
lab.task: You have 19 cans and use 6 for setup. The reserve is twice the remaining number. Also calculate the average number of cans per day over 4 days using the original count of 19. Print the whole reserve and then the average with two digits after the decimal point, separated by a space.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Find the smallest positive pulse count for a cycle size of 7 which gives both a nonzero cycle count and a nonzero remainder. Run and explain it.
criteria: Input 8 7 gives 1 1.
Input 7 7 still gives a zero remainder.

lab.title: Pulse queue
lab.task: A controller handles a fixed number of pulses per cycle. The first line of input (at most 79 bytes) gives a pulse count from 0 to 1000 and pulses per cycle from 1 to 1000. Print the number of complete cycles and pending pulses separated by a space. Keep the provided invalid output for a malformed first line.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a copy of the correct version, set extra to 0, predict the output, and test. Why could the wrong operator go unnoticed with zero?
criteria: The output is Total: 16.
Adding and subtracting zero have the same result.
The case extra = 3 distinguishes the formulas.

lab.title: Diagnose two problems in a calculation
lab.task: A shipment holds 16 base items and 3 additional items. First fix the build error in the starter. Then make it print Total: 19 by computing the result from base and extra.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Choose two valid inputs with the same quantity and price but different box capacities. Find two different packaging results and explain why the total remains the same.
criteria: For example 9 42 4 gives 2 boxes and 1 loose part, while 9 42 6 gives 1 box and 3 loose parts.
Both totals are 378 cents.
Explain the dependence on quantity and price.

lab.title: Collection receipt
lab.task: Create a three-line order receipt. The first input line (up to 79 bytes) provides quantity 0–500, unit price 0–1000 cents, and capacity 1–100 separated by whitespace. Print boxes: and the number of full boxes, loose: and the remainder, then total: and the price of all items followed by cents. Print invalid for an invalid first line.

assignments.title: Transfer a boundary check
assignments.task: Give a line containing -1 that is rejected because of its tail, then a line with the same number that is accepted. Explain the difference.
criteria: -1x fails and -1 with whitespace passes.
The explanation distinguishes the value from the record.

lab.title: An operator-entered thermometer reading
lab.task: Complete the tail check in the supplied helper. The program reads the first line with one integer from −40 to 60, allowing surrounding whitespace. Print temperature followed by the valid value. Print invalid for a rejected record.

assignments.title: Choose a neighbouring boundary case
assignments.task: With a pack size of 100, find two adjacent valid stock counts for which the answer changes.
criteria: 99 and 100 give partial.
100 and 100 give ready.

lab.title: Classify stock for packing
lab.task: Read two lines, stock and pack size, each from 0 to 100. Print invalid for invalid input or a pack size of zero. Print empty for zero stock. Otherwise print ready if stock divides exactly and partial if it leaves a remainder. Ignore input after the two records.

assignments.title: Locate an extra read
assignments.task: Predict the result for size 1, weight 4 and an extra line 999. Explain how to detect an accidental i <= boxes.
criteria: The correct result is weight 4.
The extra repetition reads 999 and unexpectedly prints invalid.

lab.title: Weigh a batch of boxes
lab.task: The first line gives a batch size from 0 to 10. Read exactly that many following lines with weights from 0 to 200. Print weight and the sum. Print only invalid if any required record is missing or invalid. Ignore input after a complete batch.

assignments.title: Explain the last repetition
assignments.task: Put 999 on the first line and a valid temperature on the second. Trace why processing ends and which value reaches the sum.
criteria: Processing stops at 999.
No value contributes to the sum. The output is empty.

lab.title: Summarise temperatures until the sentinel
lab.task: Read one record per line. A temperature is from −40 to 60. 999 ends the summary, and EOF is allowed. Accept up to eight measurements. Print invalid for an error, empty for no measurements, or the count and sum separated by a space. Ignore input after 999.

assignments.title: Module transfer task
assignments.task: Choose your own stream with a stop signal, a skip, 29 and 30. Record seen, count, sum and hot before each step and compare your trace with the output.
criteria: The trace explains termination, the skip and the boundary.
Manual calculation confirms the sum and number of hot readings.
A separate run with an invalid record confirms that there is no partial summary.

lab.title: Temperatures with skips and a scan limit
lab.task: Read at most six records, one per line. Skip −99. Stop at 999 or EOF. Ordinary temperatures run from −40 to 60 inclusive. On an error, print invalid without a partial summary. If no readings were accepted, print empty. Otherwise print three space-separated integers: the accepted count, their sum, and the count at or above 30. Ignore input after termination.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Move the definition above main in a copy and remove the separate prototype. Explain why the test still prints 12.
criteria: The definition is visible when the call is checked.
2 and 6 give 12.

lab.title: Cells in a shelf section
lab.task: Read rows and cells per row on separate lines, from 0 to 50. Keep the slot_count declaration, call and definition. Repair its calculation. Print the cell count or invalid. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Predict the outcome if the result is saved into price and price is printed twice.
criteria: 40 and 5 produce 35 35.
The original price is no longer stored separately.

lab.title: Price before and after a discount
lab.task: Read price and discount from 0 to 100 on separate lines. If discount exceeds price, print invalid. Save the result of discounted_price and print it beside the original price. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Show the starting and ending totals for trips of 2 and 4 stops before and after the fix.
criteria: Before the fix the second call goes from 6 to 18.
After the fix it goes from 0 to 12.

lab.title: Independent trips
lab.task: Enter two trips with 0 to 10 stops each. Each stop adds 3 minutes to its trip. Repair trip_minutes so calls do not share a total. Print two results or invalid. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a copy, set the threshold to 60 and design three tests around it.
criteria: 59, 60 and 61 give 0, 5 and 5.
Record all three expectations before executing.

lab.title: Bonus at the threshold
lab.task: bonus returns 5 for a score of at least 50, otherwise 0. No input is needed. Fix the comparison and confirm calls with 49, 50 and 51 using the supplied driver.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Create two direct calls before integration and check an unknown code through the main interface. Label what each test measures.
criteria: The two numerical results can be checked without stdin.
An invalid choice is rejected before calculation.

lab.title: Time and distance converter
lab.task: The first line contains code 1 or 2 and the second a magnitude from 0 to 30. Code 1 converts minutes to seconds and code 2 kilometers to meters. Fix both functions. Print seconds or meters before the result, or invalid for rejected input. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a local copy of your code in a text file. In the lesson editor, replace the power array with readings 20, 14, 6, 22 and 9. Find the last valid index and the first invalid one to its right. Restore your saved code after testing.
criteria: The length comes from the array, and 4 is the last valid index.
An input of 4 gives 9. An input of 5 gives invalid.

lab.title: Machine power by index
lab.task: Four machines have power ratings 12, 9, 15 and 4 at indices 0 through 3. Read a single integer index from the first line. Print the selected machine’s power on one line. Print invalid for a missing, malformed or out-of-range index. The supplied read_integer handles input, and any later lines are ignored. Fix the bounds check in main.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save your code to a local text file. In the lesson editor, replace readings with 6, 4, 6, 9 and 6. Keep threshold 6 and try the full length 5, the prefix of length 2, and length 0. Restore your saved code afterwards.
criteria: At the same threshold, the outputs are 4, 1 and 0 respectively.
Capacity comes from the declared array. The loop uses length.

lab.title: Active readings at or above a threshold
lab.task: The readings array contains 5, 8, 2 and 8. The first input line gives an active length from 0 to 4 inclusive. The second gives a threshold from −99 to 99. Count how many of the first length values are at least the threshold. Print the count on one line. Print invalid for a missing line, malformed integer or out-of-range value. The supplied read_integer function handles the first two lines. Further input is ignored. Fix the loop limit in count_at_least.

assignments.title: Check two repeats with your own trace
assignments.task: Enter the lines 5, 8, 5, 8, 1, 5, 5. Write the matching indices and the expected line before running.
criteria: Target 5 appears at indices 1 and 4.
The program prints 1 1 2. Explain why the second hit increases the count and leaves the first index alone.

lab.title: Three results for a reading log
lab.task: Put the number of readings, from 0 to 8, on the first line. At length 0, print the single line empty. Otherwise put each reading on its own line, followed by the target on another line. Each reading and the target must be from -99 to 99. Print the minimum, the zero-based index of the first match and the match count, separated by spaces on one line. Print -1 as the index if the target is absent. Print invalid for missing or invalid required input. The program ignores any lines after the required inputs. The starter already reads the lines and checks their ranges.

assignments.title: Check order and membership yourself
assignments.task: Enter the lines 5, 2, -2, 2, 0, -2. Write the expected lines, then compare adjacent order and the number of occurrences of each value with the output.
criteria: First line 2 -2 2 0 -2. Second line -2 -2 0 2 2.
Both lines contain two values of -2, one zero and two values of 2.

lab.title: A reading report with a sorted copy
lab.task: On the first line, enter the length from 0 to 8. At 0, print the single line empty. Otherwise enter one integer from -99 to 99 on each of the following lines. Print the original values separated by spaces on the first output line and the sorted copy on the second. Print invalid for an invalid length or a missing or invalid required value. The program ignores any lines after the required inputs. The starter already handles reading, copying by index and printing.

assignments.title: Try it on your own
assignments.task: In the lesson editor, after saving a copy of main.c in a separate text file, build label S007 from S and three digits. Write down the capacity before running.
criteria: S007 has length 4 and needs at least 5 bytes of storage.
The terminating '\0' has index 4.

lab.title: Make a numbered label
lab.task: Read the tens digit and the ones digit from separate lines. Accept values from 0 to 9. Print the letter T, then the digits in that order and the length after a space. Print invalid for an invalid number, a value out of range or a missing line. The supplied read_integer checks the numbers. The task considers the first two lines.

assignments.title: Try it on your own
assignments.task: In the lesson editor, after saving a copy of main.c in a separate text file, reduce line to three cells. Test AB, ABC and Z in that order. Check the labelled WASI cases against their expected output. Restore your saved main.c after the experiment.
criteria: The results are ok AB, long, ok Z.
In UTF-8, byte length determines the limit. Three instances of é occupy exactly six bytes.

lab.title: Read and classify complete records
lab.task: Read up to six records. Each record may hold up to six text bytes. For an ordinary line, print ok, a space and its text. Print blank for an empty line, long for one over the limit and invalid for a record with a null byte. A null byte takes the invalid status even in an overlong record. LF and CRLF do not count toward the limit. On EOF after data, handle the final record. On EOF before a new record, stop. Fix the result condition in the supplied read_line. All lengths refer to bytes.

assignments.title: Try it on your own
assignments.task: In the lesson editor, after saving a copy of main.c in a separate text file, change the dictionary to RUN and STOP and keep the limit. Check the labelled WASI cases against their expected output. Restore your saved main.c after the experiment.
criteria: RUN and STOP give known 3 and known 4.
RUN! gives unknown. Invalid length produces invalid before comparison.

lab.title: Recognize the controller keys
lab.task: Read only the first record. If it has up to eight bytes and matches OK or ADJ exactly, print known, a space and the length. Other valid text, including an empty line, gives unknown. Print invalid for an empty stream, a record longer than eight bytes or a record containing NUL. LF and CRLF separators are excluded from the length. EOF can end the final record. Keep the supplied read_line validation and correct the key comparison.

assignments.title: Try it on your own
assignments.task: In the lesson editor, after saving a copy of main.c in a separate text file, use prefix WARN, a comparison count of 4 and a limit of 8. Supply WARN ok, XWARN and WARN too long. Add another valid match after the overlong line. Check the labelled WASI cases against their expected output. Restore your saved main.c after the experiment.
criteria: The first three records produce only WARN ok, then rejected 1.
The extra match is printed in full before the total.

lab.title: Project: filter the log
lab.task: Read records until EOF. A record can hold at most 12 text bytes. Print each valid record whose first bytes are exactly ERR, preserving its text. LF and CRLF delimit records. Handle a final record with data before EOF. An overlong record or a record containing a null byte increments rejected once after it is consumed. Skip valid lines without the prefix. Finish with rejected, a space and the rejected count. Fix the selection condition and keep the supplied input reader and counter.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. Set the counters to 20 and -1 and the increment to 5. Predict and verify the result for selection 2, then restore your exercise code.
criteria: The output 20 4 preserves the left counter and updates the right counter.

lab.title: Increment the selected counter
lab.task: The left counter starts at 4 and the right at 10. Read a selection integer from the first line. Select the left counter for 1 and the right counter for 2. Add 3 through a pointer and print the two counters in their original order, separated by a space. Print invalid for any other selection or malformed input. Use the supplied read_integer. Ignore subsequent lines.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. In the editor, change the threshold to 4. Try length 3 followed by 3, 4 and 5 on separate lines. Restore your saved version afterward.
criteria: Output 2 shows that 4 and 5 both count.
The loop compares with end before accessing an element.

lab.title: Count readings through pointers
lab.task: The first line gives a reading count from 0 to 4. Read exactly that many integers from -99 to 99, one per line. Ignore later lines. Print the number of readings at least 8. Print invalid for a missing record, malformed number or length outside 0 through 4. In count_at_least, walk from the array beginning to its validated exclusive end.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. In the editor, replace the second argument of normalize with &low for one run. With input 8 and 2, explain both numbers and the returned indicator. Restore your saved code.
criteria: Output 8 2 0 shows that comparing 8 with itself is already ordered.
With the distinct addresses restored, the same input gives 2 8 1.

lab.title: Order two limits
lab.task: Read two integers from -99 to 99 on separate lines, a lower and an upper limit. The normalize function takes addresses of two live int objects, checks for NULL and swaps values only when they are out of order. Return 1 for a swap, 0 for an already ordered pair and -1 for NULL without writing. Print both values and the swap indicator separated by spaces. Print invalid for malformed input. Ignore subsequent lines.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. Change the starting response to -4. Try modes 0 and 2, then 1 and 8 on separate lines. Restore your saved version.
criteria: Failures retain -4 and print absent -4 and invalid -4. A successful read prints present 8.

lab.title: Take a snapshot of an optional reading
lab.task: Read the mode from the first line. For 0, the source is missing, so print absent 17. For 1, read a value from -99 to 99, copy it through snapshot and print present and the value. For 2, use a prepared source holding 49 and pass NULL for the output, then report the rejection as invalid 17. For malformed input print invalid. Use the supplied reader. Ignore subsequent lines.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: Save a copy of your corrected main.c in a separate text file. Change INITIAL_SAMPLE to -8, then try -9x and -9 separately. Explain why the failure check compares with the old value. Restore your saved version afterward.
criteria: The first run prints invalid and keeps -8. The second prints -9.
The code keeps no address of temporary and uses none after the function returns.

lab.title: Send a reading to the caller
lab.task: Read an integer from -99 to 99 from the first line. read_sample takes the address of a live caller-owned int, checks it for NULL, reads into a separate local integer, and copies the value into *out only after success. Return 1 after writing and 0 on failure. Print the number on success. On failure, check that the previous value is still 17 and print invalid. The supplied main uses invalid changed to flag a broken contract. Ignore subsequent lines.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Give valid input with a negative correction and a result of exactly 0. Check that the snapshot differs from the result.
criteria: 8 30 -30 gives 8 0 30. Explain why 8 30 -31 is invalid.

lab.title: Calibration log
lab.task: Use the first line, up to 63 bytes. It contains three whitespace-separated integers. Later lines are ignored. The sensor ID is 1–9999, the original reading is 0–2000 mV, and the correction is -200–200 mV. Create one record, preserve a snapshot, add the correction and check that the result is in 0–2000. Print the ID, new reading and original reading separated by spaces. Print invalid for malformed input or an out-of-range result.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Transfer the approach to a turnstile with codes 10 and 20. Specify outcomes for a repeated state and an unknown code before writing the condition.
criteria: Show a recognized transition and an unknown code on separate examples. Explain your choice of repeat behavior.

lab.title: Book issuing and return
lab.task: Read the first line, up to 63 bytes, with two integers for current and target state. Codes 1, 2 and 3 mean requested, issued and returned. Print invalid for malformed input or an unknown code. Print ok for 1 → 2 and 2 → 3, and denied for every other known pair. Input recognition is supplied. Complete can_move.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Add delivery {80, 77} to your own list. Predict the results for 77 and 80 with the correct comparison and with the original mistake.
criteria: Correct lookup leaves 77 26 for 77 and yields 80 77 for 80. Explain why looking up quantity would pick a different record.

lab.title: Delivery lookup
lab.task: The log has four records: 12 → 8, 31 → 3, 54 → 0, 77 → 26. The first line, up to 63 bytes, contains one integer ID in 1–9999. Complete the search by id. Print the ID and quantity separated by a space on a match. Print missing for a valid absent ID. Print invalid for malformed input or an out-of-range number.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Write two commands that move the same record from 1 to 3 through allowed intermediate steps. Reverse the commands and predict where the contract rejects a move.
criteria: 2 101 2 2 101 3 yields ok, ok and 101:3 203:2. Reversing order yields denied, ok and 101:2 203:2.

lab.title: Two commands for a request queue
lab.task: A store with capacity 3 initially contains 101:1 and 203:2. The first line, up to 63 bytes, contains exactly two triples of operation, ID and state. Operation 1 inserts a request only in state 1. Operation 2 advances an existing request along 1 → 2 → 3. IDs are 1–9999. A malformed line, an operation code outside 1/2, or values outside input bounds reject the entire line as invalid. The input state field accepts 0–9 syntactically; allowed operation states are 1, 2 and 3. An unknown operation state or insertion outside state 1 yields invalid for that command. Insertion checks duplicate before full. An update yields missing for an absent record and denied for a forbidden transition. Success yields ok. For a correctly parsed line print both command results followed by the records as id:state separated by spaces in array order. Complete apply by checking for an existing identifier before testing capacity.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: Use the positive even numbers 2..2×count and preserve the allocation guard.
criteria: 3 1 gives sum 12, while 3 0 still gives allocation-failed. Explain why the refusal does not depend on the summing formula.

lab.title: A bounded array
lab.task: Enter two whitespace-separated integers on the first line of up to 63 bytes: count from 1 to 16 and a flag of 0 or 1. Later lines are ignored. Complete allocate_values: a denied request or invalid size yields NULL, and an allowed size requests space for count int elements. The supplied main handles NULL. On success it stores 1 through count, prints sum N, and frees the block. Invalid input yields invalid. Flag 0 returns NULL before calling malloc.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a separate copy, also reject the calculation when count is even. Keep the shared release path.
criteria: With 4 1 the new branch rejects the computation, while released 1 remains. Name the single owner.

lab.title: Two paths, one release
lab.task: The first line of up to 63 bytes contains count from 1 to 16 and a mode of 0 or 1. The array is allocated and filled with 1 through count before the mode is checked. Mode 1 prints sum N. Mode 0 rejects the calculation and prints rejected. Both branches must free the allocated block. Complete the counter in release_values. Two cleanup calls should yield released 1. Invalid input prints invalid and released 0. If the initial malloc returns NULL, the program prints allocation-failed and released 0.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a separate copy, after resize add 3 only if the result is 1 and list.used < list.capacity. Increment used after storing the value at list.items[list.used]. Before free, print status, used, capacity, and the sum across all occupied slots.
criteria: 6 1 yields ok 3 6 14. 6 0 yields allocation-failed 2 2 11. With 2 0 there is no free slot, so the output is ok 2 2 11.

lab.title: Safe capacity changes
lab.task: The first line of up to 63 bytes contains a target capacity from 0 to 8 and a flag of 0 or 1. Malformed or out-of-range input prints invalid. The program then creates a block containing 4 and 7, with used = capacity = 2. If the initial malloc returns NULL, it prints only allocation-failed. Zero or a target below used yields invalid 2 11. Requesting the same capacity gives ok 2 11 with either flag. For a capacity change, flag 0 skips realloc and yields allocation-failed 2 11, as does an actual realloc failure. Success prints ok, the new capacity, and 11. Complete the capacity update.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a separate check set bytes = 99 and call bytes_for with width 2 and count = SIZE_MAX / 2. Reset bytes to 99 and call again with count = SIZE_MAX / 2 + 1. Do not allocate memory.
criteria: The first status is BYTES_OK and the product is stored. The second status is SIZE_OVERFLOW and bytes remains 99.

lab.title: Calculate capacity in bytes
lab.task: The first line, at most 63 bytes, contains count 0–16 and width 0–8. The special teaching input -1 2 passes SIZE_MAX and 2 to the size check without asking for a large integer. Every other pair with -1 is invalid. Print bytes N for a positive representable product, overflow for an out-of-range product, and invalid for zero or malformed input. This exercise allocates no memory.

assignments.title: Transfer the idea
assignments.task: In a separate copy of the corrected program, insert this loop after the summary printf and before destroy(&queue): for (size_t i = 0; i < queue.used; ++i) { printf("%zu:%d\n", queue.items[i].id, queue.items[i].value); } Run 20 30 2 and then 20 30 0 separately. Compare the record ids and values.
criteria: For 20 30 2, allocation-failed 2 2 30 is followed by exactly two separate lines: 1:10 and 2:20.
For 20 30 0, ok 3 4 60 is followed by lines 1:10, 2:20, and 3:30. Both fields of the first two records match. The refusal run omits 3:30.

lab.title: A resizable queue of numeric records
lab.task: The first line of up to 63 bytes contains two integer values from 0 to 9999 and a growth attempt number from 0 to 2. Each run starts with list [1:10], capacity 1, and counter 0. Mode 0 disables the controlled refusal. Modes 1 and 2 refuse the corresponding attempt before realloc. The append function assigns the next sequential id. When needed, the list doubles its capacity up to eight slots. Appending stops at the first failure. Complete the attempt counter in reserve. The main output is one line: ok or allocation-failed, followed by used, capacity, and the sum of value fields. Invalid input prints invalid. If the initial malloc returns NULL, the program prints allocation-failed alone.

assignments.title: Test a missing file without deleting the log
assignments.task: In a separate copy, temporarily request the absent input/next-shift.txt. Run with empty stdin. Restore the original path. Leave input/shift.txt present but empty in this copy, and run again.
criteria: The first run yields open-error and exit code 1. The second yields opened and exit code 0. Explain why an empty file differs from a missing file.

lab.title: Check the shift log
lab.task: A crew keeps the shift start and temperature in the fixture input/shift.txt. Leave stdin empty. Replace NULL near TODO with a call to fopen using the exact path and mode rb. Successful open and close yield opened and exit code 0. An open failure yields open-error and exit code 1 without calling fclose. A close error yields close-error and exit code 1. Leave the file contents untouched.

assignments.title: Empty input and input without a trailing LF
assignments.task: In a separate copy, clear input/route.txt without removing it. Run and download copy.txt. Then write 18 and 21 on two lines in that copy, without an LF after 21. Run and download again. Wait until the comparison is complete before saving output files to the project.
criteria: Empty input gives written 0 and a zero-byte copy.txt. Without a trailing LF, expect written 5 and hexadecimal bytes 31 38 0A 32 31.

lab.title: Copy a route for the next shift
lab.task: The stop numbers are already in input/route.txt. The program does not use stdin. Fix the loop to read until EOF, keeping every byte, including LF. The fixture ranges from 0 to 64 bytes. Write copy.txt only after successfully reading and closing the input. Success yields written N, exit code 0, and a new file. A copy of empty input exists and contains 0 bytes. Missing input yields open-input-error, and more than 64 bytes yields input-too-long. Read, write, and close errors yield their own statuses and exit code 1. The source file stays unchanged.

assignments.title: A delivery with zero quantity
assignments.task: In a separate copy replace the second row with 26 TAB 0 and LF, then with the same row followed by junk before LF. Compare the results.
criteria: The first run yields records 2 total 8. The second yields invalid line 2. Neither run creates a file.

lab.title: Validate a delivery list
lab.task: The file input/delivery.tsv contains up to 64 rows. Each row has at most 24 bytes before LF. Its ID (1–9999) and quantity (0–999) consist of ASCII digits separated by TAB. IDs are unique. Every row ends in LF. Reject CRLF, NUL, an empty row, a missing LF, a duplicate ID, or extra text. Fix the TODO in read_record. Success yields records N total S and code 0. The first invalid record yields invalid line N and code 1. An empty file yields records 0 total 0. The program reads no stdin and creates no output file.

assignments.title: The source never opens
assignments.task: In a separate copy change only the input path to input/missing-labels.txt. Keep mode 0. Predict both counter lines and check whether a result file appears.
criteria: open-input-error, then closed-input 0 and closed-output 0. Code 1. No new file.

lab.title: Copy labels for the next shift
lab.task: The fixture input/labels.txt contains label codes. Stdin selects the mode: empty or 0 means a normal copy, 1 skips output fopen, and 2 refuses the first write for nonempty input. For nonempty stdin use one digit with an optional LF. Only acquired streams are closed. Correct the input cleanup condition. Print the first failure or ok, then the number of fclose calls for each stream. Failure exits with code 1. Success exits with code 0 and an exact labels-copy.txt.

assignments.title: Failure after a successful report
assignments.task: Download the successful result, save it in the lesson project, and check the file in the editor. Then replace the second quantity with 3junk and run again. Compare this run's result list with the file previously saved to the editor.
criteria: The new run yields invalid line 2 and exit code 1. There is no new result. The saved report still contains 2 TAB 11 LF until you change it.

lab.title: A warehouse summary file
lab.task: Read input/stock.tsv using the previous lesson's rules: unique ID 1 to 9999, TAB, quantity 0 to 999, LF. Leave stdin empty. Once all rows are accepted, write the header records TAB total LF and a row N TAB S LF to stock-totals.tsv. Complete the line near TODO. Check write and close before printing ok. A malformed row yields invalid line N and exit code 1 without opening the report. Download and compare the successful result by path and bytes, then explicitly save it in the editor.

assignments.title: Check the earlier profile
assignments.task: In a copy of your solution set PACK_KIND to 0 and run with 3 again. Restore profile 1 afterward.
criteria: Profile 0 prints items=3, while profile 1 prints items=18. Identify the line that selects the value and the line that uses it.

lab.title: Convert boxes into items
lab.task: Profile 1 means 6 items in each box. Select it in packing_config.h and pass boxes to BOX_AMOUNT in main.c. The first line of stdin is exactly one digit followed by LF or end of input. Print items= followed by the number of items for valid input. Otherwise print invalid and exit with code 1.

assignments.title: Reverse the include order
assignments.task: In a copy of your solution put kit_label.h before kit.h in main.c and run with 2 again. Point out where KIT_H is first defined now.
criteria: The rebuild and parts=8 still work. Explain why the first visit now comes from kit_label.h.

lab.title: Guard the kit record
lab.task: Add a direct include of kit.h to main.c and keep kit_label.h. Protect all of struct Kit with KIT_H. Print parts= and the number of parts at four per kit. The first line of stdin is one digit followed by LF or end of input. Otherwise print invalid and exit with code 1.

assignments.title: Check the boundary of a full tray
assignments.task: Run with 6, then with 7, after predicting what changes. Repeat 7 in a copy with tray.c absent.
criteria: Expect trays=2 slots=6, then trays=3 slots=9. Without the module the build reports trays_needed before running.

lab.title: Round up to whole trays
lab.task: Pack 0 to 9 items in trays of three. In tray.c count a partially filled tray. In main.c print trays= and slots= separated by one space. Slots equal three times the tray count. The first stdin line must contain exactly one digit followed by LF or end of input. For other input print invalid and exit 1.

assignments.title: Change a price without changing the interface
assignments.task: In a copy, change only B's price to 7 in record.c. Rebuild from the three files, try B 4 and A 6, then leave record.c out of that copy.
criteria: B 4 now gives total=28 and A 6 still gives total=18. The incomplete build names the missing definition of record_total.

lab.title: Separate the console from the price calculation
lab.task: The first stdin line is A or B, a single space, and a digit, followed by LF or end of input. A costs 3, B costs 5, and quantities 0–6 are allowed. Validate the fields in record.c and calculate the total using a private helper for the unit price. Return -1 there for a rejected record. main.c prints total= and the result, or prints invalid and exits 1 for bad syntax or a rejected record.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a separate copy, use 40–60 and design a test for a faulty lower boundary.
criteria: 40 gives accepted; 39 gives invalid. The prediction identifies which comparison changes the below flag.

lab.title: A measurement at 90
lab.task: The range 30–90 is inclusive. Read the first line as a decimal integer with an optional sign and surrounding whitespace. For numeric input, write two flags to stderr and accepted or invalid to stdout. For malformed input, write only invalid to stdout. Compare your prediction with the trace at 90 and repair one condition.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a separate copy, use 5–9 and choose six inputs before running: two boundaries, their two outer neighbours, one ordinary value and one with a suffix.
criteria: 4 and 10 give invalid; 5 and 9 give valid. 7 and 7x check distinct classes.

lab.title: A booking window from 10 to 18
lab.task: Accept numbers from 10 through 18. Parse the first line as a decimal integer with an optional sign and surrounding whitespace. Print valid for valid input or invalid otherwise. Fill in a table of input classes first, then fix suffix parsing and the upper boundary. Reject lines longer than 63 bytes before the newline.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a separate copy, set limit to 12. Choose a boundary value, an outside value and malformed input to distinguish range checking from parsing.
criteria: 12 gives count 12; 13 and 12x give invalid for different reasons.

lab.title: Seat limit and separate checks
lab.task: Accept integers from 0 through 8. For a well-formed first line in range, print count and the number separated by a space. Print invalid for a rejected entry. Use limit as the sole upper bound, check a strict build if native Clang is available, and compare stdout for 0, 8 and 9.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a separate copy, use {4, 7, 9, 12}; derive count with sizeof and choose three tests at the new boundary.
criteria: 2 gives 9, 3 gives 12 and 4 gives invalid. The checks remain in the safe order.

lab.title: Three readings in a temporary array
lab.task: Parse the first line as a decimal index with an optional sign and surrounding whitespace. Indices 0–2 are valid. Print the selected value, 21, 34 or 55, or invalid. Remove the condition that allows only index 0. Keep a copy of the integer after the inner block and retain all safety checks before access.

assignments.title: Independent transfer
assignments.task: In a separate copy, use 0–9 and save one minimal input with a suffix, a valid boundary and its outer neighbour.
criteria: For example, 9x gives invalid, 9 gives slots 9 and 10 gives invalid. The log records exact stdin bytes, stdout and status for every run.

lab.title: A seat-count regression check
lab.task: Parse the first line as an integer from 0 to 30. Allow an optional sign and surrounding whitespace, and reject any other suffix. Print slots and the number with a separating space, or invalid. Record what the starter does with 12x, fix the suffix check, and keep the same input and control cases in your log.

assignments.title: One more check
assignments.task: Check ID 9999 and quantity 0 separately. Confirm that the report keeps the record and adds the final LF.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

lab.title: An unsorted tool count
lab.task: Start with records.tsv for items 42 and 7. Complete the report loop after the header. Check the agreed row order. Write down the expected stdout, stderr, status and exact file for two checks before running.

assignments.title: One more check
assignments.task: In a separate native folder, build a short main.c that constructs an Inventory in memory and calls inventory_set. Observe 1 for a present ID and 0 for an absent one. Compare both quantities as well.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

lab.title: Updating the last item on a shelf
lab.task: Implement inventory_set in inventory.c using the starter inventory for items 14 and 72. Update only existing IDs. Test the last record first and then a missing record. The build needs main.c and inventory.c.

assignments.title: One more check
assignments.task: In a fresh run invert the order of report and an invalid command. Record when the file exists and identify the failure by exit status.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

lab.title: Guard the report from a duplicate record
lab.task: The training log repeats ID 32. The starter omits the uniqueness check. Add it before appending to the array. Test the controls for an unknown ID, an invalid quantity, excess capacity and a report open failure.

assignments.title: One more check
assignments.task: Add your own regression case that fails on the starter and passes on your fix. Record its input, expected streams, status and file. Explain the limitation of wb.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

lab.title: Deliver a report for the next shift
lab.task: Fix the summary.tsv open mode in the starter, which appends a report after a stale row. Rebuild in a fresh folder and run an ordinary report, empty input, an invalid command and a repeat report. Save your own package and reopen it.
